instructions: Commerce must already be installed successfully in the same Supabase project.
Apply the private negotiation schema and deploy the cms-commerce-negotiation Edge Function.
Configure the minimum and maximum percentages and the proposal lifetime.
checks: The negotiation schema stays private to anon and authenticated Supabase roles.
Offer ownership, availability, currency, and reference price are loaded server-side from Commerce.
Buyer and seller identities come from CMS-computed identity headers or trusted Commerce data.
Proposal bounds are calculated and enforced transactionally in integer minor units.
Only one pending proposal per buyer and offer and one accepted proposal per offer can exist.
resources: Private negotiation schema and Edge Function
review: Version 1 assumes Commerce and Commerce negotiation use the same Supabase project.
An accepted proposal is an immutable price agreement; creating a Commerce order at that price requires a dedicated Commerce order capability.
Do not expose the generated API keys or service-role key to browser code.
syncNote: Commerce owns listings and orders. Commerce negotiation owns bounded proposals, decisions, and audit history.
